description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy, comparing initial accuracy, final accuracy, and the change in accuracy. The x-axis represents initial confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, marked at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents accuracy, also on a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0, marked at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are plotted: final accuracy (blue, solid line), change in accuracy (orange, dashed line), and initial accuracy (green, dotted line). The final accuracy line remains relatively stable, starting at approximately 0.9 at an initial confidence of 0.86 and ending at around 0.96 at an initial confidence of 1.00, with a slight increase and then a plateau. The change in accuracy line begins at around 0.3 at an initial confidence of 0.86, decreases to approximately 0.06 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then slightly increases to around 0.15 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The initial accuracy line starts at about 0.65 at an initial confidence of 0.86, increases to around 0.9 at an initial confidence of 0.93, remains relatively stable until an initial confidence of 0.99, and then decreases to approximately 0.75 at an initial confidence of 1.00.
